Answer: B
Reason: The CT images clearly demonstrate air within the spinal canal (pneumorrhachis), visible as a dark crescent in the posterior epidural space (Figure 2) and centrally within the dural sac (Figure 4). In the context of extensive pneumomediastinum and subcutaneous emphysema shown, this is typically a benign finding resulting from air tracking along neural foramina rather than a primary spinal pathology requiring surgery.
